questions.stem: A staff engineer at a logistics firm is prototyping an internal agent directly against the Claude API (not the Agent SDK) to reconcile shipment manifests against carrier invoices. The current implementation appends each response and any tool results to the conversation, then inspects the assistant's final text output for the substring 'RECONCILIATION COMPLETE' to decide whether to stop looping or issue another turn. During a live pilot, the agent occasionally exits early after producing partial summaries that happen to include that phrase inside a caveat sentence (e.g., 'Reconciliation complete for 40 of 52 manifests'), and it occasionally loops past 20 turns because the model rephrases the sentence. Which change would most reliably fix the loop's termination logic?

choices.text: Tighten the substring match to require the exact phrase 'RECONCILIATION COMPLETE' to appear as the first line of the response.
Terminate the loop when the API response's stop_reason field is "end_turn", and continue issuing further turns whenever it is "tool_use".
Add a hard cap of 10 turns and treat reaching the cap as successful completion, to bound worst-case latency.
Have the model emit a special final sentence such as 'STOP NOW' and detect it with a stricter parser, in addition to the existing check.

questions.explanationEn: stop_reason is the structured, authoritative termination signal the API already provides: "tool_use" means more work is expected, "end_turn" means the model considers itself done. Parsing the assistant's natural-language text for a marker phrase is fragile by construction, since ordinary caveat sentences can accidentally contain the marker and paraphrasing can cause it to be missed entirely, which is exactly what's happening here. Tightening the substring match or adding a stricter secondary parser both keep relying on this unreliable signal instead of replacing it. An iteration cap addresses worst-case latency, but treating a cap as "success" would silently truncate legitimate multi-step reconciliations rather than fixing why the loop can't tell when it's actually done.
questions.explanationJa: stop_reasonは、APIがすでに提供している構造化された正式な終了シグナルであり、"tool_use"は作業継続を、"end_turn"はモデル自身が完了したと判断したことを意味します。アシスタントの自然言語テキストから合言葉を探す方式は本質的に脆弱で、通常の注記文にたまたまその語句が含まれたり、言い換えによって検出漏れが起きたりするのは、まさに今回起きている現象です。部分文字列の一致条件を厳しくしたり、より厳格な二次パーサーを追加したりしても、この不安定なシグナルへの依存自体は変わりません。反復回数の上限は最悪ケースのレイテンシ対策にはなりますが、上限到達を「成功」として扱うと、正当な複数ステップの照合処理まで黙って打ち切ってしまい、ループが完了を正しく判定できない根本原因の解決にはなりません。

questions.stem: A market-intelligence team's multi-agent research system uses a coordinator that delegates to a web-search subagent and a financial-filings subagent. To reduce latency, an engineer configures the financial-filings subagent to call the web-search subagent directly via a shared Task invocation whenever it needs to verify a ticker symbol, bypassing the coordinator entirely. After this change, the coordinator's logs show gaps: some financial-filings failures are silently retried by the web-search subagent without ever being recorded, and the coordinator occasionally invokes web-search again on a topic already covered because it has no visibility into the cross-subagent call. What is the most effective way to fix this design?

choices.text: Give the financial-filings subagent its own retry-with-backoff logic so the undocumented calls to web-search at least fail gracefully.
Merge the two subagents into a single subagent with access to both sets of tools, so cross-calls are no longer necessary.

Route all inter-subagent communication back through the coordinator, having the financial-filings subagent return a request for verification data as part of its result so the coordinator can decide whether to invoke web-search.
Have the financial-filings subagent log its direct calls to a shared file that the coordinator reads at the end of the run to reconstruct what happened.

questions.explanationEn: Hub-and-spoke architecture requires the coordinator to manage all inter-subagent communication for observability, consistent error handling, and controlled information routing; direct subagent-to-subagent calls bypass exactly that, which is why failures and duplicate work are now invisible to the coordinator. Adding retry logic inside the subagent papers over the symptom without restoring visibility. Merging the two subagents into one sacrifices the separation-of-concerns and tool-scoping benefits of keeping specialized subagents narrow, and doesn't generalize once a third specialized subagent is added. Having the subagent log to a shared file for later reconstruction is a workaround that still doesn't let the coordinator make real-time routing or retry decisions, only a post-hoc audit.
questions.explanationJa: ハブアンドスポーク型アーキテクチャでは、可観測性・一貫したエラー処理・情報ルーティングの制御のため、サブエージェント間のあらゆる通信をコーディネーターが管理する必要があります。サブエージェント同士が直接呼び出し合うことはまさにこれを迂回しており、だからこそ失敗や重複作業がコーディネーターから見えなくなっています。サブエージェント側にリトライロジックを持たせても症状を覆い隠すだけで、可視性は回復しません。2つのサブエージェントを統合して1つにする案は、専門特化したサブエージェントを絞り込んでおく関心の分離やツールスコープの利点を犠牲にし、3つ目の専門サブエージェントが追加された際に一般化できません。共有ファイルへのログ記録は事後的な監査にはなりますが、コーディネーターがリアルタイムにルーティングやリトライを判断することはできません。

questions.stem: You are building a coordinator agent for a due-diligence research pipeline using the Claude Agent SDK. The coordinator needs to invoke three subagents — a corporate-registry lookup subagent, a litigation-history subagent, and a news-sentiment subagent — whose findings do not depend on one another. Your current implementation has the coordinator emit one Task tool call, wait for the subagent's turn to complete, inspect stop_reason, and then emit the next Task call in a subsequent turn, repeating three times sequentially. A colleague reports the pipeline takes almost three times longer than necessary. What change addresses this while preserving the coordinator's role as the single point of routing?

choices.text: Move litigation-history and news-sentiment lookups into PostToolUse hooks on the corporate-registry subagent so they fire automatically.
Give each subagent access to the other two subagents' Task definitions so they can invoke each other without coordinator involvement.
Increase max_tokens on the coordinator's requests so it can process all three subagents' outputs within one context window.
Have the coordinator emit all three Task tool calls within a single assistant turn, so the subagents execute in parallel, and then aggregate the three tool results once they return.

questions.explanationEn: Parallel subagent execution is achieved by emitting multiple Task tool calls within a single coordinator response rather than spreading them across separate turns; the three lookups are independent, so there is no need to wait for one before starting the next. Repurposing PostToolUse hooks for orchestration misuses a mechanism intended for tool-result transformation and interception, not for triggering unrelated subagent work. Letting subagents invoke each other's Task definitions reintroduces the hub-and-spoke violation of bypassing the coordinator, which harms observability and error handling. Increasing max_tokens has no effect on latency here, since the bottleneck is sequential round trips between turns, not a shortage of output space within any single turn.
questions.explanationJa: サブエージェントを並列実行するには、複数のTaskツール呼び出しを別々のターンに分けるのではなく、コーディネーターの単一の応答内でまとめて発行します。3つの調査は互いに独立しているため、1つの完了を待ってから次を始める必要はありません。PostToolUseフックをオーケストレーション目的に転用するのは、本来ツール結果の変換・介入のための仕組みを、無関係なサブエージェント処理の起動に誤用することになります。サブエージェント同士に互いのTask定義へのアクセスを与えると、コーディネーターを迂回するハブアンドスポーク違反が再発し、可観測性とエラー処理を損ないます。max_tokensを増やしても、ボトルネックは単一ターン内の出力容量不足ではなくターン間の逐次的な往復であるため、レイテンシには影響しません。

questions.stem: An internal finance-operations agent processes expense reimbursements. Company policy requires that a request never be disbursed before a manager's approval status has been confirmed through the approvals system. The current system prompt instructs the agent: 'Always call check_approval_status before calling disburse_funds.' An audit of three months of transaction logs finds 7 out of 4,200 disbursements were issued without a prior check_approval_status call in the same session, all traced to sessions where the employee mentioned their manager's name and the agent inferred approval had already happened. What is the most effective way to eliminate this failure mode going forward?

choices.text: Add a programmatic prerequisite gate that blocks the disburse_funds tool call unless check_approval_status has already returned an approved status within the same session.
Rewrite the system prompt instruction to more strongly emphasize the requirement, e.g., 'You must ALWAYS verify approval status before any disbursement, without exception.'
Add several few-shot examples showing the agent calling check_approval_status even when the employee claims their manager already approved the request verbally.
Log every disbursement without a preceding check_approval_status call to a dashboard for the finance team to review weekly.

questions.explanationEn: Financial operations require deterministic compliance guarantees, which is exactly what a programmatic prerequisite gate provides by blocking the downstream tool call at the system level rather than hoping the model follows an instruction. Both stronger prompt wording and additional few-shot examples remain probabilistic compliance mechanisms with a non-zero failure rate — which is precisely why 7 violations occurred despite an explicit instruction already existing before the audit. A weekly dashboard review is a detective control that surfaces violations after the money has already moved, rather than a preventive one that stops them from happening.
questions.explanationJa: 金融関連の操作には決定的なコンプライアンス保証が必要であり、まさにプログラム的な事前条件ゲートが、モデルが指示に従うことを期待するのではなく、システムレベルで下流のツール呼び出しをブロックすることで実現するものです。プロンプトの文言を強めることや、few-shot例を追加することは、いずれも失敗率がゼロにならない確率的なコンプライアンス手段のままであり、監査前にすでに明示的な指示があったにもかかわらず7件の違反が発生した理由もまさにそこにあります。週次ダッシュボードでのレビューは、資金がすでに動いた後に違反を発見する検知的統制であり、発生自体を防ぐ予防的統制ではありません。

questions.stem: A support-automation agent pulls order timestamps from three backend systems through separate MCP tools: the legacy order system returns Unix epoch integers, the fulfillment-partner API returns ISO 8601 strings, and the loyalty-program tool returns a custom 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:mm' string. The agent frequently miscalculates whether a return window has expired because it reasons inconsistently about these differing formats when they appear together in context. Where should the fix for this specific problem be implemented?

choices.text: A system prompt addition instructing the model to convert all timestamps to ISO 8601 in its head before comparing them.
A PostToolUse hook that converts each tool's timestamp fields into a single canonical format before the results are added to the model's context.
A few-shot example demonstrating correct return-window calculations across the three timestamp formats.
A tool_choice: "any" configuration that forces the agent to call a dedicated date-parsing tool before evaluating return eligibility.

questions.explanationEn: PostToolUse hooks are the documented mechanism for deterministically normalizing heterogeneous tool output before the model reasons over it, and timestamp-format reconciliation is exactly this kind of data-transformation problem, best solved outside the model's probabilistic reasoning. Instructing the model to mentally convert formats, or showing it a few-shot example of doing so, both still rely on the model performing consistent arithmetic and reformatting across every turn, the same class of unreliable compliance normalization hooks exist to eliminate. Forcing a separate date-parsing tool call adds an extra round trip and still leaves the actual interpretation and comparison to the model rather than fixing the data at its source.
questions.explanationJa: PostToolUseフックは、モデルが推論する前にツールの異種出力を決定的に正規化するための標準的な仕組みであり、タイムスタンプ形式の統一はまさにこの種のデータ変換問題であって、モデルの確率的な推論の外側で解決するのが最善です。モデルに頭の中で形式を変換するよう指示すること、あるいはその実演をfew-shot例として示すことは、いずれも毎ターン一貫した計算と再フォーマットをモデルが正しく行うことに依存しており、フックがまさに排除しようとしている不安定なコンプライアンスと同種のものです。専用の日付解析ツール呼び出しを強制すると往復が1回増える上、実際の解釈と比較は結局モデルに委ねられ、データそのものを発生源で修正することにはなりません。

questions.stem: A security engineer used Claude Code to trace a suspected injection vulnerability across a 40-file authentication module two days ago, ending the session with a partial call-graph of affected functions. Since then, two other engineers have merged unrelated refactors into the same module, renaming several of the functions the prior session had already traced. The security engineer wants to continue the investigation today. Which approach is most likely to produce a reliable continuation?

choices.text: Run --resume with the named prior session so the full conversation history, including all previously read file contents, is restored automatically.
Use fork_session to branch from the prior session's endpoint, so the original investigation thread remains untouched.

Start a new session and provide a structured summary of the prior findings (functions traced, call-graph edges, open questions), explicitly noting that the module has since been refactored and needs re-verification.
Resume the prior session and immediately ask Claude to re-read the entire authentication module from scratch before continuing.

questions.explanationEn: Because the underlying files changed after the session ended, the previously cached tool results — file contents and the call graph built from them — are now stale, and starting fresh with an injected structured summary is more reliable than resuming with stale tool results that no longer reflect the renamed functions. Resuming the named session restores exactly that stale content, including now-incorrect assumptions layered on top of it. fork_session is designed for exploring divergent approaches from a shared baseline that is still valid, not for recovering from a baseline whose underlying facts have since changed. Resuming and asking for a full re-read partially compensates, but the session's accumulated context still carries forward conclusions drawn before the re-read, which can bias interpretation of the new information.
questions.explanationJa: セッション終了後に対象ファイルが変更されているため、以前キャッシュされたツール結果（ファイル内容やそこから構築された呼び出しグラフ）はすでに古くなっており、構造化された要約を新しいセッションに注入して始める方が、名前変更後の関数をもはや反映していない古いツール結果を再開するより信頼できます。名前付きセッションを再開すると、まさにその古い内容と、その上に積み重なった誤った前提までもが復元されてしまいます。fork_sessionは、依然として有効な共有ベースラインから分岐したアプローチを検討するためのものであり、根拠となる事実自体が変化したベースラインからの復旧には向きません。セッションを再開して全体の再読み込みを依頼する方法は部分的な補完にはなりますが、セッションに蓄積された文脈には再読み込み前に導いた結論が引き続き残っており、新情報の解釈にバイアスを与えかねません。

questions.stem: A knowledge-management agent has two MCP tools available: search_docs, described as 'Searches documentation,' and search_kb, described as 'Searches the knowledge base.' Support engineers report that when they ask the agent to 'find the article about SSO troubleshooting,' it inconsistently calls one tool or the other, and about a third of the time it calls both, doubling latency. The underlying data sources are genuinely different: search_docs indexes versioned product manuals, while search_kb indexes support-ticket-derived troubleshooting articles. What is the most effective first step to fix the tool-selection inconsistency?

choices.text: Rename search_kb to search_kb_v2, so the model treats it as a more specific, preferred option.
Remove search_docs from the agent's available tools, and route all documentation queries through search_kb instead.
Add a routing instruction to the system prompt stating 'always prefer search_kb for troubleshooting-related queries.'
Rewrite each tool's description to state its specific content scope, example queries it's suited for, and boundary cases distinguishing it from the other tool.

questions.explanationEn: Minimal, near-identical descriptions are the root cause of unreliable selection among similar tools, so expanding each description with content scope, example queries, and explicit boundaries directly addresses why the model can't currently tell the two tools apart. Renaming the tool does nothing to clarify functional scope, since the model still has no more information about what content each tool actually covers. Removing search_docs discards a genuinely distinct, still-needed data source (versioned product manuals) rather than fixing selection between two valid tools. A keyword-sensitive system-prompt rule is a brittle patch that only helps for queries containing the word "troubleshooting" and can create unintended associations elsewhere, rather than fixing the underlying description quality that the model actually relies on for every query.
questions.explanationJa: 最小限でほぼ同一の説明文は、類似ツール間の選択が不安定になる根本原因であり、各説明文に対象範囲・想定クエリ例・他ツールとの明確な境界を追記することが、モデルが両者を区別できない理由に直接対処します。ツール名を変更しても、各ツールが実際にどの内容をカバーしているかについてモデルが得る情報は増えず、機能範囲の明確化にはなりません。search_docsを削除すると、バージョン管理された製品マニュアルという本当に別個で必要なデータソースを失うことになり、2つの有効なツール間の選択問題の解決にはなりません。キーワードに敏感なシステムプロンプトのルールは、「troubleshooting」という語を含むクエリにしか効かず、他の場面で意図しない関連付けを生みかねない脆いパッチであり、あらゆるクエリでモデルが実際に頼る説明文の質そのものを改善するものではありません。

questions.stem: A contract-review agent has a single MCP tool, analyze_document, whose description reads 'Analyzes a document and returns findings.' In practice, the agent uses this one tool for three unrelated jobs: pulling specific data points (e.g., termination clauses), producing a plain-language summary, and checking a claim against the source text. Reviewers report the tool's output format varies unpredictably from call to call, because the model has to infer, from a vague prompt each time, which of the three jobs it's supposed to be doing. What is the most effective redesign?

choices.text: Split analyze_document into three purpose-specific tools — extract_clauses, summarize_document, and verify_claim_against_source — each with its own defined input/output contract.
Keep the single tool, but add a required 'mode' parameter the model must set to one of three enum values before the tool executes.
Add few-shot examples to the system prompt showing three different ways to prompt analyze_document for the three jobs.
Increase the analyze_document description's length substantially while keeping it as one tool, detailing all three use cases in prose.

questions.explanationEn: Splitting an overloaded generic tool into purpose-specific tools with their own defined input/output contracts directly resolves the ambiguity, since each tool's schema alone communicates its job rather than requiring the model to infer intent from a vague prompt each time. Adding a required 'mode' enum is a plausible partial fix, but it still bundles three unrelated output contracts behind one tool and just relocates the disambiguation burden onto choosing the right mode value. Few-shot examples add token overhead on every call without fixing the structural ambiguity in the tool itself. Lengthening the description while keeping one tool doesn't resolve inconsistent output formats, since one tool still returns unstructured, job-dependent output regardless of how thoroughly its prose is written.
questions.explanationJa: 肥大化した汎用ツールを、それぞれ独自の入出力契約を持つ目的特化型ツールに分割することは曖昧さを直接解消します。各ツールのスキーマ自体がその役割を伝えるため、モデルが毎回曖昧なプロンプトから意図を推測する必要がなくなるからです。必須の「mode」列挙値を追加する案はもっともらしい部分的な修正ですが、依然として3つの無関係な出力契約が1つのツールに同居しており、曖昧さの解消責任を適切なmode値の選択へと移しているに過ぎません。few-shot例の追加は呼び出しごとのトークン負担を増やすだけで、ツール自体の構造的な曖昧さは解消しません。ツールを1つのまま説明文を長くしても、どれだけ丁寧に書かれていても1つのツールが役割依存の非構造化出力を返す状況は変わらず、出力形式の不整合は解消されません。

questions.stem: An MCP tool named process_return calls a backend inventory service. When the service is temporarily unreachable, when the return window has legitimately expired per policy, and when the input SKU doesn't exist, the tool currently returns the same response in all three cases: {isError: true, content: 'Operation failed'}. The agent's behavior is inconsistent: sometimes it retries a policy-expired return several times, sometimes it gives up immediately on a transient outage without retrying, and it can't explain to the customer why a request failed. What change to the tool's error responses would most directly fix this?

choices.text: Wrap every call to process_return in client-side retry logic with exponential backoff, regardless of error type.

Return structured error metadata distinguishing errorCategory (transient, validation, or business), an isRetryable boolean, and a human-readable, customer-appropriate description for each failure case.
Add a system prompt instruction telling the agent not to retry more than once on any process_return failure.
Change the tool description to list the three possible failure reasons in prose, while keeping the response format unchanged.

questions.explanationEn: Uniform 'Operation failed' responses strip the agent of the information it needs to decide whether to retry, explain a business rule to the customer, or escalate, which is exactly why its behavior is inconsistent across the three failure types; returning errorCategory and an isRetryable flag lets the agent branch correctly per case. Blanket client-side retries would retry even non-retryable business and validation errors, wasting attempts on a request that can never succeed no matter how many times it's resent. A blunt 'retry at most once' rule doesn't distinguish legitimate transient-outage retries from the expired-window case, which should never be retried at all. Changing only the tool's description leaves the runtime response format — the actual signal the agent reasons over at call time — completely unchanged.
questions.explanationJa: 画一的な「Operation failed」という応答は、エージェントがリトライすべきか、顧客にビジネスルールを説明すべきか、エスカレーションすべきかを判断するために必要な情報を奪っており、これが3種類の失敗タイプで挙動が一貫しない理由そのものです。errorCategoryとisRetryableフラグを返すことで、エージェントはケースごとに正しく分岐できるようになります。クライアント側で一律にリトライする方式は、何度再送しても絶対に成功しないリトライ不可能なビジネスエラーやバリデーションエラーまでリトライしてしまい、試行を無駄にします。「最大1回までリトライ」という乱暴なルールは、正当な一時的障害へのリトライと、そもそも一切リトライすべきでない期限切れケースを区別できません。ツールの説明文だけを変更しても、エージェントが呼び出し時に実際に推論の根拠とするランタイムの応答形式自体は何も変わりません。

questions.stem: A synthesis subagent in a research pipeline was originally scoped to two tools: combine_findings and format_citations. To handle occasional fact-checking needs, an engineer grants it the coordinator's entire toolset — 16 tools spanning web search, document retrieval, database queries, and email drafting — reasoning that more capability can only help. After this change, the synthesis subagent begins occasionally attempting unrelated actions, such as issuing raw web searches with malformed queries, and overall output quality on its core synthesis task declines. What most directly explains the regression, and what's the appropriate fix?

choices.text: The subagent's system prompt needs stronger instructions telling it not to use tools outside its intended role.
The subagent should be given tool_choice: "any", so it is forced to call a tool on every turn instead of drifting into unstructured behavior.

Access to a large, poorly scoped toolset degrades tool-selection reliability; the fix is to restrict the subagent back to a small, role-relevant set, adding only a narrowly scoped verify_fact tool for its actual fact-checking need.
The regression is unrelated to tool count; the fix is to upgrade the subagent's model to a more capable one that can handle a larger toolset.

questions.explanationEn: Granting an agent tools well outside its specialization — here, 16 tools instead of the original 2 — increases decision complexity and is documented to cause exactly this kind of misuse; the fix is scoped tool access plus a narrow, purpose-built cross-role tool for the specific high-frequency need (fact verification), rather than blanket access. Stronger system-prompt instructions are a probabilistic patch attempting to compensate for what is fundamentally an architectural scoping problem, and would need to be relied on for every one of the 16 tools indefinitely. Forcing tool_choice: "any" changes whether a tool is called on a given turn, not which tool is selected, so it doesn't address misselection among an oversized toolset. Treating this as a model-capability problem misdiagnoses the cause; a stronger model given the same 16 tools still faces the same increased selection complexity.
questions.explanationJa: 本来の専門範囲を大きく超えるツール（ここでは元の2つから16個へ）をエージェントに与えると意思決定の複雑さが増し、まさにこの種の誤用を引き起こすことが知られています。修正策は、特定の高頻度ニーズ（事実確認）のために狭くスコープされた専用ツールを1つ追加しつつ、サブエージェントを役割に関連する小さなツールセットに戻すことであり、包括的なアクセス権付与ではありません。システムプロンプトの指示を強化する方法は、本質的にはアーキテクチャ上のスコープ設計の問題を確率的なパッチで補おうとするものであり、16個すべてのツールについて永続的にこの指示への依存に頼ることになります。tool_choice: "any"を強制しても、あるターンでツールが呼ばれるかどうかが変わるだけで、どのツールが選ばれるかは変わらないため、過大なツールセットの中での誤選択は解決しません。これをモデルの能力の問題として扱うのは原因の誤診断であり、より高性能なモデルであっても同じ16個のツールを与えられれば同様に選択の複雑さの増大に直面します。

questions.stem: A platform team wants every engineer on their repository to automatically get access to a shared Jira MCP server when they clone the repo, authenticated via a token that must never be committed to version control. Separately, one senior engineer wants to experiment with a personal, still-unstable MCP server for a side project without affecting teammates. How should these two be configured?

choices.text: Configure both servers in .mcp.json, but add a comment noting the experimental one is not yet production-ready.
Configure the Jira server with the token hardcoded in .mcp.json, since the repository is private, and configure the experimental server the same way in a personal fork.
Configure both servers in ~/.claude.json, so that neither is accidentally shared with the team until they're both confirmed stable.

Configure the Jira server in the project's .mcp.json with the token referenced via environment variable expansion (e.g., ${JIRA_TOKEN}), and have the engineer configure their experimental server in their user-level ~/.claude.json.

questions.explanationEn: Project-scoped .mcp.json is for shared team tooling and supports environment variable expansion specifically so credentials don't need to be committed, while user-scoped ~/.claude.json is for personal or experimental servers that shouldn't affect teammates — matching each server to its correct scope satisfies both requirements. Putting both in .mcp.json still commits a token to version control regardless of an explanatory comment, and exposes the unstable experimental server to every teammate who clones the repo. Hardcoding the token directly in .mcp.json is exactly the practice environment variable expansion exists to prevent, and a private repository doesn't eliminate the risk of credential exposure through history, forks, or CI logs. Putting both servers in ~/.claude.json fails the actual requirement that every engineer automatically receive the Jira server on clone, since user-level configuration is never shared via version control.
questions.explanationJa: プロジェクトスコープの.mcp.jsonはチーム共有ツール向けであり、認証情報をコミットせずに済むよう環境変数展開（例：${JIRA_TOKEN}）に対応しています。一方、ユーザースコープの~/.claude.jsonは、チームメイトに影響を与えたくない個人用・実験用サーバー向けです。それぞれを正しいスコープに割り当てることで両方の要件を満たせます。両方を.mcp.jsonに設定すると、説明コメントを付けてもトークンがバージョン管理にコミットされる状態は変わらず、不安定な実験用サーバーもリポジトリをクローンした全メンバーに公開されてしまいます。トークンを.mcp.jsonに直接ハードコーディングするのは、まさに環境変数展開が防ごうとしている行為そのものであり、プライベートリポジトリであっても履歴・フォーク・CIログを通じた認証情報漏洩のリスクはなくなりません。両方を~/.claude.jsonに設定すると、クローン時に全エンジニアが自動的にJiraサーバーへアクセスできるという本来の要件を満たせません。ユーザーレベルの設定はバージョン管理を通じて共有されることがないためです。

questions.stem: While refactoring a utility function, Claude Code's Edit tool call fails with an error indicating the anchor text it was given matches four separate locations in the file, none of which is unique enough to target reliably. The file is 1,800 lines long, and the same helper pattern is repeated with minor variations throughout. What is the most reliable way to proceed with this specific modification?

choices.text: Use Read to load the full file contents, construct the corrected version in full, and use Write to replace the file.
Retry the same Edit call with the identical anchor text, since transient tool failures are common and a second attempt often succeeds.
Use Grep to search for the anchor text across the codebase to identify a more unique substring, then retry Edit with a longer anchor sourced only from Grep's matching line.
Switch to Glob to locate all files matching the utility function's naming pattern, then apply the edit to each matching file individually.

questions.explanationEn: When Edit cannot find unique anchor text, Read followed by Write is the documented, reliable fallback for targeted modifications in files where surrounding context doesn't disambiguate the intended location. Simply retrying the identical Edit call ignores that this isn't a transient failure — the ambiguity is structural (four genuinely similar locations) and will recur identically on retry. Searching with Grep for a longer anchor sourced only from the single matching line doesn't guarantee uniqueness, since the four locations already share near-identical surrounding text; disambiguating reliably would require examining more surrounding context than a single matched line provides, which is effectively what Read does anyway. Glob solves a different problem — finding files by name pattern — and has no bearing on disambiguating one of four locations within a single already-identified file.
questions.explanationJa: Editが一意なアンカーテキストを見つけられない場合、周囲の文脈だけでは対象箇所を特定できないファイルにおける対象を絞った修正には、Readで読み込んでからWriteで置き換える方法が信頼できる標準的な代替策です。同一のEdit呼び出しを単純に再試行しても、これが一時的な失敗ではないという事実を無視することになります。曖昧さは構造的なもの（本当に似た4箇所が存在する）であり、再試行しても同じ結果が繰り返されます。Grepで一致した1行のみから得たより長いアンカーで検索しても、4箇所がすでにほぼ同一の周囲テキストを共有しているため一意性は保証されません。信頼できる形で判別するには、一致した1行以上の周囲の文脈を確認する必要があり、それは事実上Readが行っていることと同じです。Globはファイル名パターンによるファイル検索という別の問題を解決するものであり、すでに特定済みの1つのファイル内にある4箇所のうちどれかを判別することとは関係がありません。

questions.stem: A tech lead is surprised that a newly onboarded contractor keeps committing directly to main and skipping the linter step, despite these being described as 'always enforced by Claude Code' during onboarding. Checking the repository, the project-level CLAUDE.md contains only a short paragraph about the tech stack and says nothing about commit conventions or linting. The tech lead's own machine, however, has a detailed ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md listing exactly those two rules, which is why the tech lead never noticed the problem. What is the most effective fix?

choices.text: Ask the contractor to copy the tech lead's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md file into their own home directory.

Move the commit and linting conventions from the tech lead's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md into the project-level CLAUDE.md (or a project .claude/rules/ file), so they're version-controlled and apply to every contributor.
Add a note at the top of the project README asking new contributors to manually configure their local CLAUDE.md according to team conventions.
Have the tech lead's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md reference the contractor's account via an @import statement, so the rules propagate automatically.

questions.explanationEn: User-level CLAUDE.md settings apply only to the individual user and are never shared with teammates via version control, which is exactly why the contractor never received them despite the rules genuinely existing on the tech lead's machine; moving shared conventions into project-level configuration (or .claude/rules/) is the structural fix that makes them apply automatically to every contributor, including future ones. Asking the contractor to manually copy the file is a one-off workaround that won't stay in sync as the rules evolve and doesn't scale past one contractor. A README note relies on manual, error-prone human compliance rather than automatic, version-controlled propagation — the same category of failure that caused the original problem. An @import referencing another user's account isn't a supported mechanism; user-level configuration files aren't shared or cross-referenceable between accounts at all.
questions.explanationJa: ユーザーレベルのCLAUDE.md設定は個々のユーザーにのみ適用され、バージョン管理を通じてチームメイトと共有されることは決してありません。これこそが、テックリードのマシンにはルールが実在していたにもかかわらず、契約社員がそれを一度も受け取らなかった理由です。共有すべき規約をプロジェクトレベルの設定（またはproject .claude/rules/）に移すことが構造的な修正であり、これにより将来参加するメンバーも含め、すべての貢献者に自動的に適用されるようになります。契約社員に手動でファイルをコピーしてもらう方法は一時的な対処に過ぎず、ルールが進化しても同期が保たれず、契約社員が複数になった場合にはスケールしません。READMEに注記を追加する方法は、手動で誤りが起きやすい人間の遵守に依存しており、まさに元の問題を引き起こしたのと同じ種類の失敗要因です。他のユーザーのアカウントを参照する@importは、そもそもサポートされている仕組みではありません。ユーザーレベルの設定ファイルはアカウント間で共有も相互参照もされません。

questions.stem: A team builds a /audit-deps skill that scans package manifests, cross-references known vulnerabilities, and produces a long itemized report. Two problems have emerged: first, running the skill floods the main conversation with hundreds of lines of intermediate scanning output, making it hard to continue the actual task afterward; second, the skill occasionally attempts to modify files directly when it shouldn't, since its only job is to report findings, not fix them. Which two SKILL.md frontmatter configurations most directly address these two problems, respectively?

choices.text: argument-hint to prompt for which manifest file to scan, and context: fork to prevent file modification.
allowed-tools restricted to read-only tools to isolate verbose output, and argument-hint to prevent file modification.
context: fork to isolate the verbose scanning output in a sub-agent context, and allowed-tools restricted to read-only tools to prevent file modification.
A project-scoped command in .claude/commands/ instead of a skill, combined with allowed-tools restricted to read-only tools.

questions.explanationEn: context: fork runs a skill in an isolated sub-agent context specifically to prevent verbose or exploratory output from polluting the main conversation, which directly addresses the first problem, while allowed-tools restricts which tools a skill can invoke during execution, directly preventing the unwanted file-write attempts described in the second problem. The other pairings mismatch mechanism to problem: argument-hint only prompts for missing invocation arguments and has no bearing on either output isolation or tool restriction. Swapping the skill for a project-scoped slash command doesn't help either, since slash commands don't support context: fork or allowed-tools frontmatter at all, so the isolation problem would remain unsolved even with tool restrictions in place.
questions.explanationJa: context: forkは、詳細な出力やメイン会話を汚染する探索的な出力を防ぐために、スキルを分離されたサブエージェントの文脈で実行する仕組みであり、これが1つ目の問題に直接対処します。一方allowed-toolsは、スキル実行中に呼び出せるツールを制限するもので、2つ目の問題である意図しないファイル書き込みの試みを直接防ぎます。他の組み合わせは仕組みと問題が噛み合っていません。argument-hintは呼び出し時に不足している引数を尋ねるだけで、出力の分離にもツール制限にも関係がありません。スキルの代わりにプロジェクトスコープのスラッシュコマンドに置き換える案も役に立ちません。スラッシュコマンドはそもそもcontext: forkやallowed-toolsのフロントマターに対応していないため、ツール制限を行っても出力分離の問題は未解決のままです。

questions.stem: An infrastructure-as-code repository has Terraform files spread across a dozen service directories (services/api/main.tf, services/worker/main.tf, services/billing/network.tf, and so on), and the team wants every .tf file to follow the same resource-tagging and naming conventions regardless of which service directory it lives in. Placing a CLAUDE.md file in each of the twelve directories works but is tedious to keep in sync when the convention changes. What is the more maintainable alternative?

choices.text: Consolidate the convention into the root-level CLAUDE.md under a heading titled 'Terraform Conventions,' relying on Claude to recognize when it's relevant.
Create a .claude/skills/terraform-conventions skill that must be manually invoked before editing any .tf file.
Symlink a single shared CLAUDE.md file into each of the twelve service directories.
Create a single .claude/rules/ file with YAML frontmatter specifying paths: ["**/*.tf"], so the convention loads automatically whenever a matching file is being edited, regardless of directory.

questions.explanationEn: Glob-pattern rules in .claude/rules/ apply a convention by file type wherever matching files exist, which is the documented advantage over directory-level CLAUDE.md files for conventions that span multiple directories, and it means updating the convention requires editing exactly one file. Consolidating into the root CLAUDE.md relies on inference from a large, always-loaded file rather than deterministic, path-scoped activation, and adds irrelevant Terraform context to every unrelated task in the repository. A skill that must be manually invoked contradicts the goal of the convention being applied automatically whenever a .tf file is touched. Symlinking a shared file into twelve directories is a filesystem-level workaround that's fragile compared to a first-class scoping mechanism, and still requires maintaining twelve symlinks correctly as the repository structure evolves.
questions.explanationJa: .claude/rules/内のglobパターンによるルールは、該当するファイルが存在する場所を問わずファイル種別ごとに規約を適用でき、これは複数ディレクトリにまたがる規約に対してディレクトリレベルのCLAUDE.mdより優れている点として文書化されています。規約を更新する際もファイル1つを編集するだけで済みます。ルートのCLAUDE.mdに統合する方法は、常時読み込まれる大きなファイルからClaudeが関連性を推測することに依存しており、決定的でパスに紐づいた有効化にはならず、リポジトリ内の無関係なあらゆる作業にもTerraformの文脈が余分に加わってしまいます。手動で呼び出す必要があるスキルは、.tfファイルを編集するたびに自動的に規約が適用されるという目標と矛盾します。共有ファイルを12個のディレクトリにシンボリックリンクする方法は、一級のスコープ機構と比べて脆いファイルシステムレベルの回避策であり、リポジトリ構造が変化するたびに12個のシンボリックリンクを正しく維持し続ける必要があります。

questions.stem: Two tasks arrive on the same day. Task one: rename a utility function used in six files, where every call site is unambiguous and a project-wide search confirms there are no dynamic or reflective references to the old name. Task two: choose between two viable approaches for adding real-time notifications to the product — WebSockets versus Server-Sent Events — which will affect the infrastructure, several existing services, and future scalability. Which combination of approaches is most appropriate?

choices.text: Direct execution for the rename, since it is well-scoped with a clear, verified set of call sites; plan mode for the notifications decision, since it involves architectural tradeoffs and infrastructure implications.
Plan mode for both tasks, since any change touching multiple files benefits from an exploration phase first.
Direct execution for both tasks, since Claude Code can revert changes if the notifications approach turns out to be wrong.
Plan mode for the rename, since it touches six files, and direct execution for the notifications decision, since Claude can explore both options as it implements.

questions.explanationEn: Plan mode is designed for tasks with architectural implications and multiple valid approaches, while direct execution suits simple, well-scoped changes with a verified, unambiguous set of call sites — the deciding factor is architectural complexity and reversibility, not raw file count. Applying plan mode to both tasks adds unnecessary overhead to a rename that's already fully understood and confirmed unambiguous by a project-wide search. Treating both as direct execution risks costly rework on the notifications decision, since infrastructure and multi-service changes are exactly the kind of hard-to-reverse architectural commitment plan mode's upfront exploration exists to prevent. Reversing the mapping — plan mode for the six-file rename and direct execution for the architectural decision — applies overhead where it isn't needed and skips it where the actual tradeoffs and unknowns exist.
questions.explanationJa: プランモードは、アーキテクチャ上の影響があり複数の有効なアプローチが存在するタスクのために設計されており、直接実行は、範囲が明確で検証済みの呼び出し箇所を持つ単純なタスクに適しています。判断基準はファイル数そのものではなく、アーキテクチャ上の複雑さと後戻りのしやすさです。両方のタスクにプランモードを適用すると、すでに完全に理解され、プロジェクト全体の検索で曖昧さがないと確認済みのリネーム作業に不要なオーバーヘッドを加えることになります。両方を直接実行として扱うと、通知機能の判断で高コストな手戻りのリスクを負うことになります。インフラや複数サービスにまたがる変更は、まさにプランモードの事前探索が防ごうとしている、後戻りしにくいアーキテクチャ上の決定そのものだからです。対応関係を逆にする案（6ファイルのリネームにプランモード、アーキテクチャ上の決定に直接実行）は、不要な箇所にオーバーヘッドをかけ、実際にトレードオフと未知数が存在する箇所ではそれを省いてしまいます。

questions.stem: A developer asks Claude Code to implement a caching layer for an internal pricing service, but hasn't yet decided on an invalidation strategy, how to handle partial cache corruption, or what should happen if the underlying pricing source is temporarily unavailable during a cache miss. Rather than specifying all of this upfront, which approach is most likely to surface these considerations before implementation begins?

choices.text: Ask Claude to write the caching layer immediately, then review the generated code line by line to identify any decisions it made implicitly.
Ask Claude to first interview you with clarifying questions about invalidation strategy, corruption handling, and fallback behavior, before writing any code.
Provide 2-3 concrete input/output examples of cache reads and writes, so Claude can infer the invalidation and fallback behavior from the examples.
Ask Claude to write a comprehensive test suite for the caching layer first, then implement the code to satisfy the tests.

questions.explanationEn: The interview pattern — having Claude ask clarifying questions before implementing — is specifically suited to surfacing design considerations the developer hasn't yet anticipated in an unfamiliar or underspecified domain, which is exactly the situation described here. Writing the code first and reviewing it afterward is reactive rather than preventive, and risks silently committing to unstated defaults buried in the implementation rather than surfacing them as explicit decisions beforehand. Concrete input/output examples work well when the transformation itself is well-understood but described inconsistently in prose; they don't surface undecided architectural questions like invalidation strategy, since there's no example to construct until that strategy exists. Test-driven iteration is powerful once behavior is already defined, but here the fallback and invalidation behavior itself hasn't been decided, so there's nothing concrete yet to write tests against.
questions.explanationJa: 実装前にClaudeに確認質問をさせるインタビュー・パターンは、開発者がまだ想定していない設計上の考慮事項を、不慣れであったり仕様が曖昧だったりする領域で表面化させるのに特に適しており、まさに今回の状況に当てはまります。先にコードを書いてから後で確認する方法は事後対応であり、実装内部に埋もれた未表明のデフォルト挙動を、事前の明示的な意思決定として表面化させないまま黙って確定させてしまうリスクがあります。具体的な入出力例は、変換ロジック自体はよく理解されているが自然言語による説明が一貫していない場合には有効ですが、無効化戦略のような未決定のアーキテクチャ上の問題を表面化させることはできません。その戦略自体が存在しない限り、例を作りようがないからです。テスト駆動の反復は、挙動がすでに定義されている場合には強力ですが、ここではフォールバックと無効化の挙動自体がまだ決まっていないため、テストを書く対象となる具体的なものがまだ存在しません。

questions.stem: A CI pipeline runs Claude Code twice on every pull request: once using the same session that generated an auto-fix commit, to also review that commit for correctness, and once more on each subsequent push to the PR, without providing the results of the prior review run. The team notices two issues: the self-review rarely flags problems with the auto-generated fix, and each new push re-reports issues that were already commented on and dismissed by a human reviewer as intentional. What two changes would most directly address these two issues, respectively?

choices.text: Increase max_tokens on the review session so it has more room to catch its own mistakes, and re-run the entire review from scratch on every push for consistency.
Add --output-format json to the review invocation so findings are machine-parseable, and rerun the fix-generation session an extra time before reviewing.

Run the review in a fresh, independent Claude Code session rather than the one that generated the fix, and include the prior review's findings in context so the agent reports only new or still-unaddressed issues.
Use the -p flag to run the review non-interactively, and instruct the model in the system prompt to 'be more critical of its own prior work.'

questions.explanationEn: An independent review session lacks the generator's reasoning context and is documented as more effective at catching subtle issues than self-review, which addresses the first problem; separately, including prior review findings in context and instructing the model to report only new or still-unaddressed issues is the documented fix for the duplicate-comment noise on subsequent pushes, addressing the second. Increasing max_tokens doesn't address either root cause, since token budget isn't what's causing self-review blindness, and re-running from scratch on every push is exactly what produces the duplicate-comment problem. --output-format json improves machine-parseability, not self-review bias, and rerunning fix-generation an extra time doesn't fix a review problem at all. The -p flag is necessary for automation generally but doesn't fix self-review bias, and instructing the same biased session to 'be more critical' still relies on unreliable self-correction within the same reasoning context rather than an independent instance.
questions.explanationJa: 独立したレビューセッションは、生成時の推論の文脈を引き継いでおらず、自己レビューよりも巧妙な問題を発見するのに効果的であることが分かっており、これが1つ目の問題への対処になります。別の対策として、以前のレビュー結果を文脈に含め、新規または未対応の課題のみを報告するよう指示することが、後続のプッシュで重複コメントのノイズが発生する2つ目の問題に対する文書化された解決策です。max_tokensを増やしても、トークン予算不足が自己レビューの盲点の原因ではないため根本原因への対処にはならず、毎回のプッシュで最初からレビューをやり直すことこそが重複コメント問題を引き起こしています。--output-format jsonは機械可読性を高めますが自己レビューのバイアスには関係なく、修正生成セッションを追加でもう一度実行してもレビューの問題は解決しません。-pフラグは自動化一般に必要ですが自己レビューのバイアスは解消せず、同じバイアスのかかったセッションに「自身の過去の作業にもっと批判的になれ」と指示しても、独立したインスタンスではなく同じ推論文脈内での不確実な自己修正に頼ることになります。

questions.stem: An automated code-review prompt currently instructs Claude to 'only report high-confidence, important issues and avoid noisy findings.' Despite this instruction, developers report the review still flags many minor stylistic preferences as if they were bugs, while occasionally missing a real off-by-one error. The team wants to meaningfully reduce false positives without suppressing genuine bug reports. What change to the prompt is most likely to work?

choices.text: Strengthen the existing wording to 'only report extremely high-confidence issues that you are absolutely certain are bugs.'
Lower the model's temperature setting for the review call, so its judgments become more consistent between runs.
Ask the model to assign a numeric confidence score to each finding, and filter out any finding below a 90% confidence threshold before reporting.

Replace the vague confidence-based instruction with explicit categorical criteria defining exactly which issue types must be reported (e.g., logic errors, security issues) versus which must be skipped (e.g., naming preferences, formatting), with concrete code examples for each category.

questions.explanationEn: General instructions like 'be conservative' or confidence-based filtering don't improve precision the way specific, categorical criteria do, because the model has no shared, well-calibrated notion of 'high confidence' to filter against, whereas concrete criteria and worked examples give it an actual decision boundary to apply consistently. Strengthening the same vague wording is the same failure mode restated more forcefully, not a structural fix. Lowering temperature affects output variability between runs, not the underlying criteria being applied, so it wouldn't stop the model from consistently misclassifying style preferences as bugs. Asking for a numeric self-reported confidence score reintroduces exactly the unreliable proxy the exam guide warns about — the model isn't well-calibrated enough for an arbitrary numeric threshold to reliably separate genuine bugs from stylistic nitpicks.
questions.explanationJa: 「保守的に」といった一般的な指示や確信度に基づくフィルタリングは、具体的で分類ベースの基準ほど精度を向上させません。モデルには、それに照らしてフィルタリングできるような、共有され適切に較正された「高い確信度」という概念が存在しないためです。一方、具体的な基準と実例は、モデルが一貫して適用できる実際の判断境界を与えます。同じ曖昧な文言をより強く言い換えても、同じ失敗パターンをより強い表現で繰り返しているだけで、構造的な修正にはなりません。temperatureを下げることは実行間の出力のばらつきに影響しますが、適用される基準そのものには影響しないため、モデルがスタイルの好みを一貫してバグと誤分類することを止められません。数値による自己申告の確信度スコアを求める案は、まさに試験ガイドが警告している信頼性の低い代理指標を再導入することになります。任意の数値しきい値で本物のバグとスタイル上の些細な指摘を確実に区別できるほど、モデルは較正されていません。

questions.stem: A support-ticket triage agent must choose one of five categories (Billing, Technical, Account Access, Feature Request, Other) for each incoming ticket, but many tickets plausibly fit two categories at once — for example, 'I was charged twice after my password reset locked me out of billing settings' touches both Billing and Account Access. Detailed prose instructions describing each category's boundaries have not resolved the model's inconsistent choices on these ambiguous tickets. What is the most effective next step?

choices.text: Add several few-shot examples of genuinely ambiguous tickets, each showing which category was chosen and a brief rationale for why it was chosen over the plausible alternative.
Add a sixth category called 'Ambiguous' that the model can select whenever a ticket plausibly fits more than one category.
Expand the prose description of each category with more adjectives distinguishing it from the others.
Instruct the model to always pick the category mentioned first in the ticket text, since customers tend to state their primary concern first.

questions.explanationEn: Few-shot examples that demonstrate reasoning for choosing one action over a plausible alternative are specifically effective for ambiguous-case handling, since they let the model generalize the underlying judgment to new, unseen ambiguous tickets rather than matching only cases explicitly listed. Adding an 'Ambiguous' category avoids making the actual routing decision, which is likely not useful to whatever downstream team or workflow consumes the category. Expanding the prose description has already effectively been tried, since detailed boundary descriptions are stated to not have resolved the inconsistency — the problem isn't a missing adjective, it's a lack of demonstrated judgment on edge cases. Picking whichever category is mentioned first is an arbitrary heuristic unrelated to which concern actually drives the customer's issue, and would misclassify tickets that lead with a secondary complaint before their primary one.
questions.explanationJa: もっともらしい代替案よりもある行動を選んだ理由を示すfew-shot例は、曖昧なケースの扱いに特に効果的です。明示的に挙げられたケースだけを模倣するのではなく、根底にある判断を未見の曖昧なチケットへと一般化できるようになるためです。「Ambiguous」というカテゴリを追加する案は、実際のルーティング判断を回避するだけで、そのカテゴリを利用する後続のチームやワークフローにとってはおそらく有用ではありません。説明文を拡充する案はすでに実質的に試されており、詳細な境界説明を用いても不整合が解消しなかったと明記されています。問題は形容詞の不足ではなく、境界事例に対する判断の実例が示されていないことです。最初に言及されたカテゴリを選ぶという方法は、顧客の問題を実際に左右している事情とは無関係な恣意的なヒューリスティックであり、主要な問題より先に副次的な不満を述べたチケットを誤分類してしまいます。

questions.stem: An invoice-processing pipeline extracts structured line items from scanned invoices using tool_use with a strict JSON schema. After deployment, the pipeline reliably produces syntactically valid JSON for every invoice, but a monthly audit finds 4% of processed invoices have line items that don't sum to the stated invoice total, and a handful have the tax amount recorded in the subtotal field. What should the team conclude, and what's an appropriate response?

choices.text: The schema itself must be malformed, since a properly defined JSON schema would prevent both syntax and semantic errors; the fix is to tighten the schema's field types.

Strict JSON schemas via tool use eliminate syntax errors but not semantic errors; the team should add a semantic validation step, such as comparing a calculated_total field against the stated total, and route discrepancies for correction or review.
The extraction tool should be replaced with plain-text prompting and manual JSON parsing, since tool_use is evidently not achieving reliable structured output.

Since the JSON is syntactically valid 100% of the time, the 4% of arithmetic mismatches are most likely caused by inconsistent tool_choice configuration, and should be fixed by switching to tool_choice: "any".

questions.explanationEn: Tool use with a JSON schema guarantees schema-compliant syntax, but has no bearing on whether the extracted values are semantically correct relative to one another; the documented pattern is to add explicit semantic checks, such as a calculated-versus-stated-total comparison, rather than expecting the schema alone to catch arithmetic inconsistencies. Concluding the schema is malformed misunderstands what JSON schemas actually validate — field types and structure, not cross-field arithmetic relationships that only a runtime check can verify. Abandoning tool_use for plain-text prompting and manual parsing is a regression to a strictly worse approach that would reintroduce the syntax errors tool_use had already eliminated, on top of not fixing the semantic issue either. Attributing the mismatches to tool_choice configuration misdiagnoses the cause; tool_choice governs whether and which tool is called, not the semantic correctness of values within an already well-formed call.
questions.explanationJa: JSONスキーマを伴うツールユースはスキーマに準拠した構文を保証しますが、抽出された値同士が意味的に整合しているかどうかには関係しません。文書化されているパターンは、計算合計と申告合計を比較するといった明示的な意味検証ステップを追加することであり、スキーマだけで算術的な不整合を検出できると期待することではありません。スキーマが不完全だと結論づけるのは、JSONスキーマが実際に検証するもの（フィールドの型や構造）と、実行時チェックでしか確認できないフィールド間の算術的関係を混同しています。tool_useをやめてプレーンテキストのプロンプトと手動のJSON解析に置き換えることは、tool_useがすでに解消していた構文エラーを再発させるだけの明確な後退であり、意味的な問題も解決しません。不整合の原因をtool_choiceの設定に帰する考え方は誤診断です。tool_choiceはツールが呼ばれるかどうか、どのツールが呼ばれるかを制御するものであり、すでに正しく整形された呼び出し内の値の意味的な正しさには関係しません。

questions.stem: A document-extraction pipeline validates each extraction against a Pydantic schema and retries with the validation error appended to the prompt when a check fails. Two categories of validation failures appear in the logs: about 60% are cases where a date field was returned in an unexpected string format that the schema rejects, and about 40% are cases where a required 'contract_end_date' field is empty because the source document simply never states an end date (it's an evergreen contract). The team currently retries every failure up to three times. What change would most improve both reliability and efficiency?

choices.text: Increase the retry limit from three to six attempts across the board, since some evergreen contracts may eventually be parsed correctly with enough attempts.
Remove contract_end_date from the schema entirely, since a meaningful fraction of documents don't contain this field.

Keep the retry-with-error-feedback loop for format-related failures, but make contract_end_date nullable in the schema, and stop retrying when the failure reason is a genuinely missing value rather than a format mismatch.
Apply the same retry-with-error-feedback strategy uniformly to both categories, since consistent handling simplifies the pipeline.

questions.explanationEn: Retries are effective for structural or format mismatches, where the model can correct its own output given specific feedback, but ineffective when the required information is genuinely absent from the source document — no number of retries will conjure a date that was never written down; making the field nullable prevents the model from being forced to fabricate a value just to satisfy a required field. Raising the retry limit wastes additional compute retrying a case that can never succeed regardless of attempt count. Removing the field entirely discards a legitimately useful value for the majority of contracts that do specify an end date, an overcorrection driven by the evergreen-contract minority. Applying the identical retry strategy to both categories ignores that they have fundamentally different, documented handling: retry-and-correct for the format mismatches, and nullable-and-accept for genuinely missing values.
questions.explanationJa: リトライは、モデルが具体的なフィードバックをもとに自身の出力を修正できる構造上・形式上の不整合には効果的ですが、必要な情報がそもそも元文書に存在しない場合には効果がありません。何度リトライしても、書かれたことのない日付が生成されることはないからです。フィールドをnullable（null許容）にすることで、必須フィールドを満たすためだけにモデルが値を捏造させられる事態を防げます。リトライ上限を引き上げても、試行回数に関わらず絶対に成功しないケースに追加の計算資源を浪費するだけです。フィールドを完全に削除する案は、実際に終了日を明記している大多数の契約にとって有用な値を失わせるものであり、少数の永久契約に引きずられた過剰な対処です。両カテゴリに同一のリトライ戦略を適用する案は、両者が本質的に異なる文書化された扱い方（形式不整合には再試行して修正、真に欠落した値にはnull許容として受け入れる）を持つことを無視しています。

questions.stem: A compliance team runs two Claude-powered processes: a nightly job that re-classifies roughly 50,000 historical support tickets against an updated policy taxonomy for a report reviewed the next business day, and an in-app process that classifies each new ticket the instant a customer submits it, so the live queue can route it to the right team immediately. The team is evaluating whether to move both to the Message Batches API for its 50% cost savings. Which evaluation is correct?

choices.text: Move both processes to the Message Batches API, since the 50% cost savings apply regardless of workload, and any latency difference can be absorbed with a sufficiently large worker pool.
Keep both processes on the synchronous API, since the Message Batches API does not support the multi-turn tool calling that either process might need in the future.

Move the live per-ticket classification to the Message Batches API for the cost savings, and keep the nightly job synchronous, since it processes a much larger volume that benefits from immediate results.

Move the nightly re-classification job to the Message Batches API, since its latency tolerance (reviewed the next business day) comfortably absorbs the batch API's up-to-24-hour processing window; keep the live per-ticket classification on the standard synchronous API.

questions.explanationEn: The Message Batches API offers substantial cost savings, but no guaranteed latency SLA and a processing window of up to 24 hours, making it well-suited to a non-blocking, latency-tolerant workload like a next-business-day report, and inappropriate for a live path that gates immediate queue routing on a response. Applying it to both regardless of workload ignores that no worker pool size compensates for the batch API's lack of a per-request latency guarantee; a live customer-facing classification simply cannot wait an indeterminate amount of time. Keeping both on the synchronous API out of caution about multi-turn tool calling forfeits real, available savings on the nightly job, which doesn't require multi-turn tool calling in the first place. Moving the live classification to batch and keeping the nightly job synchronous inverts the correct mapping, applying the latency-tolerant API to the latency-sensitive workload and vice versa.
questions.explanationJa: Message Batches APIは大幅なコスト削減をもたらしますが、レイテンシに関するSLAの保証はなく、処理には最大24時間かかる可能性があります。そのため、翌営業日に確認されるレポートのような非ブロッキングでレイテンシ許容度の高いワークロードには適していますが、応答を条件に即座にキューをルーティングするライブパスには不向きです。ワークロードにかかわらず両方に適用する案は、どれだけワーカープールを大きくしてもバッチAPIの1リクエストあたりのレイテンシ保証の欠如を補えないことを無視しています。顧客対応のライブ分類は、不確定な時間を待つことができません。マルチターンのツール呼び出しへの懸念から両方を同期APIのままにする案は、そもそもマルチターンのツール呼び出しを必要としない夜間ジョブにおける実際に得られるはずのコスト削減を放棄することになります。ライブ分類をバッチに移し夜間ジョブを同期のままにする案は対応関係が逆であり、レイテンシ許容度の高いAPIをレイテンシに敏感なワークロードに、その逆をレイテンシ許容度の高いワークロードに適用してしまっています。

questions.stem: A team automates release-note generation: the same Claude Code session that just implemented a batch of bug fixes is then prompted, in the same conversation, to 'review your changes above for any regressions before we ship.' Over several releases, this self-review step has caught formatting issues but has never once caught a functional regression, even when regressions were later found by human QA. What does the exam guide's research on review architectures suggest is happening, and what's the recommended fix?

choices.text: A model that retains its own generation reasoning in context is less likely to question its own decisions; an independent Claude instance without that reasoning context should perform the review instead.
The self-review step is working correctly; the team should simply add more explicit instructions asking it to 'think harder' about possible regressions.
The issue is that the self-review step runs without extended thinking enabled; enabling extended thinking within the same session would resolve it.
The self-review step should be replaced with a larger, more capable model within the same session, since a stronger model is less prone to confirmation bias.

questions.explanationEn: This is the documented self-review limitation: a model retains reasoning context from generation, making it less likely to question its own decisions in the same session, and independent review instances without that prior context are more effective at catching subtle issues — exactly the pattern observed across releases where formatting was caught but functional regressions never were. Assuming the step is 'working correctly' and just needs stronger instructions asks the same biased session to overcome a structural bias through wording alone, which the repeated failures across releases directly contradict. Extended thinking still occurs within the same session and the same accumulated reasoning context, so enabling it doesn't confer the independence that actually fixes the blind spot. Swapping in a larger model within the same session still carries forward the same generation reasoning trail, so a stronger model doesn't address the structural cause of the self-review blind spot, only its raw capability.
questions.explanationJa: これは文書化されている自己レビューの限界です。生成時の推論の文脈を保持しているモデルは、同じセッション内で自身の判断に疑問を持ちにくく、その以前の文脈を持たない独立したレビューインスタンスの方が、巧妙な問題を発見する上でより効果的です。まさに、リリースを重ねてもフォーマットの問題は発見できても機能的な回帰は一度も発見できなかったというパターンに合致します。このステップが「正しく機能している」だけで、より強い指示さえ加えればよいと考えるのは、同じバイアスのかかったセッションに対して文言だけで構造的なバイアスを克服させようとするものであり、複数のリリースにわたる繰り返しの失敗がそれを直接否定しています。拡張思考を有効にしても、同じセッションと同じ蓄積された推論文脈の中で行われることに変わりはないため、実際に盲点を解消する独立性を与えることにはなりません。同じセッション内でより大きなモデルに差し替えても、同じ生成時の推論の流れを引き継いだままであるため、より強力なモデルであっても自己レビューの盲点の構造的原因には対処できず、純粋な能力の向上にしかなりません。

questions.stem: A customer-support agent handles a 45-minute chat session involving a refund request. Midway through, the conversation-management layer compresses the first half of the transcript into a short summary to save tokens. By the end of the session, the agent tells the customer their refund will be $84.50, but the customer had explicitly stated early in the conversation that the correct amount, per a manager's prior verbal approval, was $94.50 — a detail that was compressed away as 'customer discussed refund amount' in the summary. What is the most effective structural fix to prevent this class of error?

choices.text: Increase the token budget allocated to the conversation summary, so more of the original detail is retained in prose form.

Extract specific transactional facts (amounts, dates, order numbers, prior approvals) into a persistent 'case facts' block that is included in every prompt outside the summarized history, rather than letting them be compressed along with the rest of the conversation.
Disable summarization entirely, and always pass the full, unabridged transcript on every turn regardless of length.
Instruct the summarization step to 'preserve all numbers mentioned in the conversation,' as part of its prompt.

questions.explanationEn: Progressive summarization risks condensing numerical values and customer-stated expectations into vague prose, which is exactly what happened to the $94.50 approval; extracting transactional facts into a separate, persistent structured block sidesteps summarization's lossy compression entirely for the details that matter most. Increasing the summary's token budget only makes the same lossy, prose-based compression somewhat less lossy, with no guarantee any specific figure survives. Disabling summarization entirely reintroduces the token-budget problem summarization exists to solve, and doesn't scale to longer or multi-issue sessions. Instructing the summarization step to preserve all numbers still relies on a probabilistic generation step to reliably follow that instruction every time, which is the same class of unreliable compliance that caused the original loss.
questions.explanationJa: 段階的な要約には、数値や顧客が明言した期待事項が曖昧な文章へと圧縮されてしまうリスクがあり、まさに94.50ドルの承認額に起きたことがそれです。取引に関する事実を独立した永続的な構造化ブロックに抽出することで、最も重要な詳細については要約による情報損失を完全に回避できます。要約に割り当てるトークン予算を増やしても、同じ文章ベースの圧縮による情報損失がやや軽減されるだけで、特定の数値が必ず残る保証はありません。要約を完全に無効化すると、要約がそもそも解決しようとしていたトークン予算の問題が再燃し、長時間または複数案件にまたがるセッションには対応できません。「会話中のすべての数値を保持せよ」と要約ステップに指示しても、その指示を毎回確実に守るかどうかは依然として確率的な生成処理に依存しており、これはまさに今回の情報損失を引き起こしたのと同じ種類の不確実なコンプライアンスです。

questions.stem: A customer messages a support agent: 'My order is delayed and I really need it by Friday for a family event — is there any way to expedite shipping?' The company's written policy addresses standard delay compensation (credits, refunds) but says nothing about expediting shipment as a goodwill gesture for personal circumstances. The customer has not asked to speak to a human. What is the most appropriate action for the agent to take?

choices.text: Offer the standard delay compensation (credit or refund) as a substitute, since it's the closest policy-covered remedy available, and close out the conversation.
Autonomously approve an expedited shipment on the agent's own judgment, since the customer's request seems reasonable and low-risk.
Escalate to a human agent, since the request falls into a genuine policy gap — expediting for personal circumstances — rather than a scenario the written policy actually addresses either way.
Ask the customer to explicitly confirm they want to speak to a human before escalating, since they didn't request escalation themselves.

questions.explanationEn: Appropriate escalation triggers include policy exceptions and gaps, not just complex cases or explicit customer requests, and this request sits squarely in a gap the policy is silent on — exactly the kind of case that should route to a human with the authority to make or decline an exception. Offering standard compensation instead silently substitutes a remedy the customer didn't actually ask for and understates the agent's genuine uncertainty about whether expediting is possible, rather than surfacing that uncertainty appropriately. Autonomously approving the request oversteps the agent's authority on something the policy doesn't address, risking inconsistent, ungoverned exceptions across customers. Requiring the customer to explicitly confirm they want a human adds an unnecessary step; a policy gap is itself a sufficient escalation trigger regardless of whether the customer explicitly asked to speak to a person.
questions.explanationJa: 適切なエスカレーションのトリガーには、複雑なケースや顧客からの明示的な要求だけでなく、ポリシーの例外や欠落も含まれます。今回の依頼は、まさにポリシーが沈黙している欠落部分に該当し、例外を認めるか却下するかの権限を持つ人間へルーティングすべき典型的なケースです。標準的な補償を代わりに提示する対応は、顧客が実際には求めていない救済策を黙って差し替えるものであり、迅速発送が可能かどうかについてエージェントが実際に抱える不確実性を適切に表面化させず、かえって曖昧にしてしまいます。エージェントが自らの判断で自律的に依頼を承認することは、ポリシーが触れていない事項について権限を逸脱する行為であり、顧客ごとに一貫性のない統制されない例外を生むリスクがあります。顧客に「人間と話したいか」を明示的に確認させてからエスカレーションする方法は不要な手順であり、ポリシーの欠落自体が、顧客が明示的に人間との対話を求めたかどうかにかかわらず、十分なエスカレーションのトリガーとなります。

questions.stem: In a multi-agent research pipeline, a document-analysis subagent searches an internal repository for filings related to a small, newly founded company and returns zero results, because the company genuinely has no filings on record yet. Separately, on a different run, the same subagent times out while querying the repository for a different company due to a network issue. Both cases currently return the coordinator an identical status: {result: [], status: 'no_data'}. What problem does this create, and how should it be fixed?

choices.text: The subagent should retry internally up to five times on any zero-result response before returning to the coordinator, regardless of whether the cause was a timeout or a genuinely empty result.
The coordinator should always treat a 'no_data' status as a coverage gap and note it in the final report, regardless of the underlying cause.
The subagent should suppress the timeout case entirely and simply omit that company from the final report, since surfacing an error to the coordinator adds unnecessary complexity.

The coordinator cannot distinguish a legitimate empty result from an access failure that might succeed on retry; the subagent should return distinct signals — a successful empty result versus a structured failure with failure type and what was attempted — so the coordinator can decide whether to retry, proceed, or flag a coverage gap.

questions.explanationEn: Conflating access failures, which may warrant a retry or an alternative approach, with valid empty results, which represent a successful query that simply found nothing, hides information the coordinator needs to make an appropriate recovery decision; returning structured, distinct signals for each case is the documented fix. Retrying every zero-result response internally, including the genuinely empty case, wastes attempts on a query that can never produce different data no matter how many times it's repeated. Always treating 'no_data' as a coverage gap mislabels the newly founded company's search — which succeeded and legitimately found nothing — as an unexplained failure in the final report. Suppressing the timeout and simply omitting the company is the 'silently suppressing errors' anti-pattern the guide explicitly warns against, hiding a real, possibly recoverable failure from the coordinator entirely.
questions.explanationJa: リトライすれば成功する可能性のあるアクセス障害と、単に何も見つからなかった正当な空の結果とを混同すると、コーディネーターが適切な復旧判断を下すために必要な情報が失われます。それぞれについて構造化された別個のシグナルを返すことが、文書化された修正方法です。真に空の結果を含め、すべてのゼロ件応答を内部で最大5回までリトライする方法は、何度繰り返しても絶対に異なるデータを生み出せないクエリに試行を浪費することになります。「no_data」を常にカバレッジの欠落として扱う方法は、成功はしたが正当に何も見つからなかった新設企業の検索を、最終報告書の中で説明のつかない失敗として誤ってラベル付けしてしまいます。タイムアウトを抑制してその企業を最終報告書から単純に省く方法は、ガイドが明示的に警告している「エラーを黙って抑制する」というアンチパターンであり、実際には回復可能かもしれない障害をコーディネーターから完全に隠してしまいます。

questions.stem: An engineer uses Claude Code in one long-running session to explore an unfamiliar 200,000-line codebase, identifying which classes implement a plugin interface. After roughly ninety minutes of continuous exploration in the same session, the engineer notices Claude begins giving inconsistent answers about which classes it already found, and starts describing 'typical' plugin patterns instead of the specific classes it discovered earlier in the session. What combination of changes would most directly address this?

choices.text: Have Claude maintain a scratchpad file recording confirmed findings as they're discovered, and delegate further exploration to subagents that report back concise summaries rather than continuing to accumulate raw discovery output in the main session.
Increase max_tokens for each individual turn, so Claude has more room to restate its earlier findings in full each time.
Ask Claude to re-read the entire codebase from the beginning once inconsistencies are noticed, to refresh its understanding.
Switch to a model with a larger context window, so the same single-session exploration pattern can continue for longer before degradation occurs.

questions.explanationEn: This is the documented pattern for context degradation during extended exploration sessions: a scratchpad file persists key findings across context boundaries, and subagent delegation isolates verbose discovery output so the main session's context isn't consumed by raw exploration detail, directly counteracting the described symptoms of inconsistent, 'typical pattern' answers. Increasing per-turn max_tokens expands output capacity but does nothing to prevent the underlying degradation caused by a context window filling with undifferentiated exploration history. Re-reading the entire codebase from scratch is expensive and doesn't prevent the same degradation from recurring later in an even longer session, since it doesn't change how findings are being persisted. Switching to a larger-context model delays the same failure mode rather than addressing its cause — the fix is architectural (scratchpad plus delegation), not simply a bigger context window applied to the same accumulation pattern.
questions.explanationJa: これは、長時間にわたる探索セッションにおけるコンテキスト劣化に対する文書化されたパターンです。スクラッチパッドファイルはコンテキストの境界を越えて重要な発見事項を保持し、サブエージェントへの委譲は詳細な探索出力を切り離すことで、メインセッションのコンテキストが未整理の探索詳細で消費されるのを防ぎます。これにより、記述された「一貫性のない回答」や「典型的なパターン」を語り出すという症状に直接対処できます。ターンごとのmax_tokensを増やすと出力容量は広がりますが、未整理の探索履歴でコンテキストウィンドウが埋まっていくという根本的な劣化を防ぐことにはなりません。コードベース全体を最初から読み直す方法はコストが高く、発見事項の保持方法自体は変わらないため、さらに長いセッションで同じ劣化が再発するのを防げません。より大きなコンテキストを持つモデルへの切り替えは、原因への対処ではなく同じ失敗モードを先送りするだけであり、修正はアーキテクチャ上のもの（スクラッチパッドと委譲の組み合わせ）であって、同じ蓄積パターンに単に大きなコンテキストウィンドウを当てはめることではありません。

questions.stem: An extraction pipeline for vendor invoices reports 97% overall field-level accuracy across a six-month sample, and the finance team is considering removing human review entirely for high-confidence extractions to cut turnaround time. Before doing so, an analyst breaks the same sample down by document type and finds accuracy is 99.2% for standard single-page invoices, but only 81% for multi-currency invoices with embedded credit memos, a document type that makes up 6% of volume. What should this finding change about the plan to remove human review?

choices.text: Nothing — since multi-currency invoices are only 6% of total volume, their lower accuracy has a negligible effect on the 97% aggregate figure and can be safely ignored.

Human review should be retained for multi-currency invoices with embedded credit memos (and any other segments shown to underperform), even as review is reduced for well-performing segments like standard single-page invoices.
The 97% aggregate figure should be treated as unreliable, and the entire pipeline should be rebuilt from scratch before any review changes are considered.
Human review should be removed for all document types, but the confidence threshold used to flag extractions for review should be raised uniformly across all types.

questions.explanationEn: Aggregate accuracy metrics can mask meaningfully worse performance on specific document types, and the correct response is to validate accuracy by segment before automating away human review, keeping review in place specifically where a segment underperforms while still reducing it elsewhere. Dismissing the finding because multi-currency invoices are a small share of volume is exactly the failure mode the guide warns about — a low-volume segment's poor accuracy doesn't need to move the aggregate number much to represent a real, costly error rate for the specific transactions and customers in that segment. Treating the aggregate figure as unreliable and rebuilding the entire pipeline overreacts to a segment-specific finding, when the well-performing 94% of volume doesn't require rebuilding. Raising a uniform confidence threshold across all document types doesn't correct for the multi-currency segment's specifically worse underlying accuracy the way segment-aware routing would, since a single threshold applied uniformly still treats structurally different error rates as if they were the same.
questions.explanationJa: 全体の精度指標は、特定の文書タイプにおける実質的に悪い性能を覆い隠すことがあり、正しい対応は人によるレビューを自動化で置き換える前にセグメントごとに精度を検証することです。性能が悪いセグメントについてはレビューを維持しつつ、他のセグメントではレビューを縮小します。多通貨請求書が全体量のわずか6%であることを理由にこの発見を軽視することは、まさにガイドが警告している失敗パターンです。低ボリュームのセグメントの精度の低さは、全体の数値をそれほど動かさなくても、そのセグメントに属する特定の取引や顧客にとっては実質的でコストのかかるエラー率を意味します。全体の数値を信頼できないと判断してパイプライン全体を作り直すことは、セグメント固有の発見に対する過剰反応であり、良好な性能を示す94%のボリュームについては作り直す必要がありません。すべての文書タイプに一律の確信度しきい値を引き上げる方法は、セグメントを意識したルーティングとは異なり、多通貨セグメント特有の低い精度を是正できません。単一のしきい値を一律に適用することは、構造的に異なるエラー率をあたかも同じであるかのように扱い続けることになるからです。

questions.stem: A synthesis subagent in a market-research pipeline combines findings from two credible industry reports on the same metric — one states the global market grew 14% year-over-year, the other states 9% — without noting that the first report's data was collected six months before the second's, during a period the second report separately describes as an unusual demand spike. The final synthesized output presents a single blended estimate of 'approximately 11.5% growth' with no indication that the two source figures disagreed or why. What is the most effective fix?

choices.text: Instruct the synthesis subagent to always defer to whichever source has the more recent publication date, and discard the older figure entirely.
Instruct the synthesis subagent to average the two figures whenever they disagree by less than 10 percentage points, and flag a conflict only above that threshold.

Require subagents to preserve both figures with source attribution and publication/collection dates in their structured output, and have the synthesis step explicitly annotate the conflict and its likely temporal explanation, rather than blending the numbers into a single value.
Remove both figures from the report and replace them with a qualitative statement that the market 'grew during the period,' since the specific numbers are in dispute.

questions.explanationEn: The correct pattern for conflicting statistics from credible sources is to annotate the conflict with source attribution rather than arbitrarily selecting or blending one value, and requiring publication or collection dates prevents a genuine temporal difference — a demand-spike period versus a later, more normal period — from being misread as a plain contradiction. Always deferring to the more recent source discards potentially still-relevant information and assumes recency alone resolves the disagreement, when here the disagreement is actually explained by a temporary spike rather than either source simply being wrong. The blended-average approach, which is what the scenario describes actually happening, manufactures a figure that doesn't represent either source's real finding and obscures the more informative explanation — the temporal demand spike — entirely. Removing both numbers discards specific, sourced information that report readers would find valuable, when the better fix is to present both figures with their dates and context rather than stripping them out.
questions.explanationJa: 信頼できる情報源から得た矛盾する統計に対する正しいパターンは、恣意的に一方の値を選んだり両者を平均したりするのではなく、出典を明示した上で矛盾に注記を付けることです。公表日または収集日を必須とすることで、需要急増期と、その後のより通常の期間という本物の時間的な差異が、単純な矛盾として誤読されるのを防げます。常により新しい情報源を優先する方法は、依然として有用かもしれない情報を切り捨て、新しさだけで不一致が解消すると仮定していますが、実際にはこの不一致は一時的な急増によって説明されるものであり、どちらかの情報源が単に誤っているわけではありません。10ポイント未満の差なら平均するという方法は、まさにこのシナリオで実際に起きていることであり、どちらの情報源の実際の結果も表さない数値を作り出し、より有益な説明である一時的な需要急増という事実を完全に覆い隠してしまいます。両方の数値を削除する方法は、報告書の読者にとって価値のある具体的で出典のある情報を失わせるものであり、より良い修正策は数値を取り除くのではなく、日付と文脈とともに両方の数値を提示することです。

questions.stem: An engineer builds a codebase-migration agent that processes each of 140 files in a legacy module using a fixed three-step prompt chain: read the file, rewrite it to the new API, run its unit test. This works well for most files, but roughly 15 files define shared interfaces that other files depend on, and changing those in isolation silently breaks callers that the per-file chain never revisits. What change to the agent's decomposition strategy would most directly fix this?

choices.text: Increase the number of unit tests run per file, so breakages in dependent files are caught earlier.
Keep the fixed three-step chain for every file, but run all 140 files in parallel instead of sequentially, to surface failures faster.
Move to adaptive decomposition: after the per-file pass, run a separate cross-file consistency pass that specifically re-checks callers of any shared interface that was modified.
Add a fourth fixed step, 'update dependents,' to the same per-file chain, run immediately after each file's rewrite.

questions.explanationEn: A fixed prompt chain applied uniformly per file cannot detect cross-file breakage because each file is treated as an independent unit of work; the documented fix is adaptive decomposition that adds a dedicated cross-file integration pass on top of the per-file pass, specifically targeting files affected by shared-interface changes. Running more unit tests per file only strengthens the same per-file-isolated view and still never revisits callers in other files. Parallelizing the same fixed chain changes execution speed, not what work is actually being done, so it doesn't address the missing cross-file check. Adding a fourth step to the per-file chain still evaluates each file in isolation immediately after its own rewrite, before all the shared-interface files have even finished migrating, so it can't reliably catch breakage from changes made later in the run.
questions.explanationJa: ファイルごとに一律に適用される固定プロンプトチェーンでは、各ファイルが独立した作業単位として扱われるため、ファイル横断的な破壊を検出できません。文書化された修正策は、ファイル単位のパスに加えて、共有インターフェースの変更によって影響を受けたファイルを特に対象とする専用のクロスファイル統合パスを追加する、適応的な分解です。ファイルごとの単体テストを増やしても、同じファイル単位の孤立した見方が強化されるだけで、他ファイルの呼び出し元を再確認することにはなりません。同じ固定チェーンを並列化しても実行速度が変わるだけで、実際に行われる作業内容は変わらないため、欠落しているクロスファイルチェックには対処できません。ファイル単位のチェーンに4番目のステップを追加しても、自身の書き換え直後という各ファイルが孤立した時点で評価されるため、共有インターフェースを持つ他のファイルがまだ移行を終えていない段階では、後で行われる変更による破壊を確実には捉えられません。
